section: India - Peninsular drainage: east-flowing and west-flowing rivers, river basins, watershed
subsections: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the largest left-bank tributary of the Godavari?
accepted.x: Pranhita is the largest left-bank tributary of the Godavari. It is formed by the Wardha and Wainganga rivers and joins the Godavari near Kaleshwaram.
accepted.tq: Use the size clue to distinguish the major tributary from other left-bank tributaries.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Indravati — Godavari
2. Tel — Mahanadi
3. Kabini — Krishna
4. Tungabhadra — Krishna
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Indravati is a tributary of the Godavari, while Tel and Tungabhadra are tributaries of the Mahanadi and Krishna respectively. Kabini is a right-bank tributary of the Kaveri, not the Krishna.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the easily confusable river–tributary pair.

accepted.s: With reference to the Godavari, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Pravara, Manjira and Manair are its right-bank tributaries.
Purna, Pranahita and Sabari are its right-bank tributaries.
Tungabhadra is its largest left-bank tributary.
Tel is its principal right-bank tributary.
accepted.x: Pravara, Manjira and Manair join the Godavari from the right bank. Purna, Pranahita, Indravati and Sabari are its important left-bank tributaries.
accepted.tq: Test the left-bank and right-bank classification directly.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:

List-I (River)
a. Bhima
b. Kabini
c. Tel
 d. Hemavathi

List-II (Main river)
i. Kaveri
ii. Mahanadi
iii. Krishna
iv. Krishna

Codes:
accepted.x: Bhima is a left-bank tributary of the Krishna; Kabini and Hemavathi are tributaries of the Kaveri; and Tel is a right-bank tributary of the Mahanadi.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair Kabini–Kaveri and eliminate incompatible codes.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Ghataprabha is a right-bank tributary of the Krishna. Tungabhadra is also a right-bank tributary, Sheonath is a left-bank tributary of the Mahanadi, and Bhavani is a right-bank tributary of the Kaveri.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched river and bank among reversed bank classifications.

accepted.s: Vedavathi, formed by the Veda and Avathi streams in the Bababudangiri hills, is a right-bank tributary of which river?
accepted.x: Vedavathi is a right-bank tributary of the Tungabhadra and joins it at Siruguppa.
accepted.tq: Use the tributary–sub-tributary relationship rather than confusing it with a direct Krishna tributary.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the east-flowing rivers of Peninsular India is correct?
o: They generally form large deltas at their mouths.
They invariably flow through rift valleys and form estuaries.
They all originate in the Eastern Ghats.
They are short and swift and are mainly used for natural harbours.
accepted.x: East-flowing rivers generally drain into the Bay of Bengal and form large deltas. West-flowing rivers more commonly form estuaries and support hydropower and natural harbours.
accepted.tq: Use the mouth feature to separate east-flowing rivers from west-flowing rivers.
accepted.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of west-flowing rivers?
accepted.x: Narmada, Tapi, Sabarmati and Mahi flow westwards towards the Arabian Sea. The other groups contain east-flowing rivers.
accepted.tq: Classify the entire group by its drainage direction before examining individual rivers.
accepted.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Narmada flows through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.
2. Tapi flows through a rift valley between the Satpura and Ajanta ranges.
3. Both Narmada and Tapi form large deltas at their mouths.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Narmada and Tapi flow through rift valleys, but as west-flowing rivers they generally form estuaries rather than large deltas.
accepted.tq: Identify the false statement by reversing the characteristic mouth of west-flowing rivers.
accepted.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following rivers is the longest west-flowing river of India?
accepted.x: Narmada is the longest west-flowing river, with a length of about 1,312 km. Tapi is the second longest at about 724 km.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the longest river from the second-ranked river using the stated lengths.
accepted.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Tapi river reaches the Arabian Sea at which of the following places?
o: Kandla near the Gulf of Kachchh
Diu near the Gulf of Khambhat
accepted.x: The Tapi reaches the sea at Suvali near Surat. It is the second longest west-flowing peninsular river and runs through a rift valley.
accepted.tq: Use the precise mouth location to distinguish Tapi from other west-flowing rivers.
accepted.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following rivers crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat?
accepted.x: The Mahi crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice and ultimately reaches the Gulf of Khambhat.
accepted.tq: Combine the unusual numerical crossing fact with the destination to identify the river.
accepted.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an inland-drainage river?
accepted.x: Luni is an inland-drainage river that ends in the Rann of Kutch. Other inland-drainage rivers listed include Machhu, Rupen, Saraswati, Banas and Ghaggar.
accepted.tq: Recognise the river that does not reach the sea but terminates in an inland basin.
accepted.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Luni ends in the Rann of Kutch.
2. Banas is an east-flowing river originating in the Aravallis.
3. Sahibi is a north-flowing river originating in the Aravallis.
4. Sabarmati is a west-flowing river originating in the Aravallis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Aravallis give rise to west-flowing Luni and Sabarmati, east-flowing Banas and north-flowing Sahibi; Luni ends in the Rann of Kutch.
accepted.tq: Use directional classification to verify each Aravalli-born river.
accepted.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Approximately how many small rivers drain the west coast of India?
accepted.x: About 600 small rivers drain the west coast. These rivers are generally short and swift and commonly form estuaries.
accepted.tq: Retain the approximate figure rather than confusing it with the lengths of major rivers.
accepted.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Peninsular rivers in descending order of their lengths:
A. Mahanadi
B. Tapi
C. Godavari
D. Narmada
accepted.x: The descending order is Godavari (1,465 km), Narmada (1,312 km), Mahanadi (858 km) and Tapi (724 km).
accepted.tq: Arrange by the numerical hierarchy, starting with the longest river and ending with the shortest.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the longest Peninsular rivers in descending order?
accepted.x: The order is Godavari (1,465 km), Krishna (about 1,400 km), Narmada (1,312 km), Mahanadi (858 km) and Tapi (724 km).
accepted.tq: Compare adjacent river lengths instead of relying only on whether they flow east or west.

accepted.s: The Narmada and Son rivers originate from which of the following places?
accepted.x: Both the Narmada and Son originate at Amarkantak in the Maikal range of Madhya Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Link the common source with the two rivers rather than selecting a source associated with only one river.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Krishna rises at Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats, at the Krishna Kund. The Godavari rises at Trimbakeshwar, Mahanadi at Sihawa and Tapi at Multai.
accepted.tq: Match each river with its distinctive source and eliminate the swapped-source pairs.

accepted.s: The source of the Kaveri is located at which of the following places?
o: Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu
accepted.x: The Kaveri rises at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu, Karnataka. Nandi hills are associated with the origin of the Pennar.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely located Karnataka source regions of Kaveri and Pennar.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Krishna originates at Mahabaleshwar. The Brahmagiri hills at Talakaveri are the source of the Kaveri.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped source by comparing the Western Ghats source points.

accepted.s:
Which of the following rivers originate in the Eastern Ghats?
1. Vamsadhara
2. Nagavali
3. Machkund
4. Sileru
5. Sabari
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Vamsadhara, Nagavali, Machkund, Sileru and Sabari are all listed as rivers originating in the Eastern Ghats.
accepted.tq: When every listed item belongs to the same source region, select the complete combination.

accepted.s: The river Tapi originates at which of the following places?
o: Multai in the Satpura plateau of Betul district
accepted.x: The Tapi rises at Multai, near Betul, in the Satpura plateau of Madhya Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the precise source locality to distinguish Tapi from Narmada, Mahanadi and Kaveri.

accepted.s: The Western Ghats are called the ‘Water Tower of Peninsular India’ mainly because they provide the sources of which group of rivers?
accepted.x: The Western Ghats are described as the Water Tower of Peninsular India because they provide the sources of the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri river systems.
accepted.tq: Connect the descriptive geographical title with the river systems originating in the region.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about west-flowing rivers is correct?
o: They are generally short and swift and are suitable for hydropower generation.
They generally have long courses and form extensive deltas.
They invariably terminate in inland salt lakes.
They flow only through the Eastern Ghats.
accepted.x: West-flowing rivers are generally short and swift, form estuaries rather than deltas and are suitable for hydropower. Their estuaries also support natural harbours on the west coast.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete characteristic combination of west-flowing rivers.
accepted.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Narmada — Marble Rocks and Dhuandhar Falls near Jabalpur
accepted.x: Luni is an Aravalli-born desert river that ends in the Rann of Kutch, not the Gulf of Khambhat. Narmada, Tapi and Periyar are correctly matched with the other descriptions.
accepted.tq: Use the destination trap to distinguish inland-drainage Luni from west-flowing rivers reaching the sea.
accepted.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only left-bank tributaries of the Mahanadi and Godavari respectively?
o: Hasdeo and Tel; Pranahita and Manair
Tel and Sheonath; Pravara and Manjira
Sheonath and Hasdeo; Purna and Indravati
Sheonath and Tel; Sabari and Pravara
accepted.x: Sheonath and Hasdeo are left-bank tributaries of the Mahanadi, while Purna and Indravati are left-bank tributaries of the Godavari. Tel is a right-bank tributary of the Mahanadi, and Pravara and Manjira are right-bank tributaries of the Godavari.
accepted.tq: Check the bank classification separately for each main river before combining the pairs.
